title: Veal Piccata
description:
Here’s a pretty simple, but tasty, dish. It gets its perkiness from the combination of fresh lemon juice and capers, mixed with some white wine and chicken broth (and, of course, garlic). But watch out with the lemon juice. Most recipes call for too much lemon and this can then get to be quite tart. (If this happens, you could try the advice that I once offered to Aunt Judy.
Just add more butter – that always helps!)
As with so many of these dishes, you can substitute veal with chicken, pork tenderloin filet slices, or fish – cooking these a little longer than the very thinly sliced veal.
Be sure to make some simple starch, such as buttered noodles, a cheesy ravioli, or even mashed potatoes, to soak up the delicious sauce. A plain green vegetable is also nice.
Because this dish is so easy to make, it’s a good one to whip up quickly after a dance at a Museum (if you don’t knock any pictures off the wall!) or after a successful Squeezebox installation.
directions: Deglaze the pan with wine and bring to a boil, scraping to remove any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
When the wine has been reduced by half, add the chicken stocks, chopped garlic, capers, and 2 tablespoons of the lemon juice. Cook for 5 minutes.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until very hot, but not smoking, and then add 2 tablespoons of butter (maybe also a peeled garlic clove to make everything smell a little better).
Flour and cook the veal slices until golden brown on both sides, about 1 minute per side.
Transfer to a dish in a warm oven and then repeat the process with the remaining slices. If necessary, add a little more oil or butter as you’re cooking.
Whisk in the remaining 4 tablespoons butter and chopped parsley. Carefully add more salt or lemon juice to taste.
When the butter has melted, return the veal scallops to the pan and cook until heated through and the sauce has thickened, about 1 minute or so.
Garnish with parsley sprigs and serve immediately.
Be sure not to trip over any high-tech music installations!
